key_insight: One resident base plus 1-bit sign deltas fused into the GEMM serves thousands of full fine-tunes, so memory per extra tenant falls to ~1/16 of a model copy.
killer_doubt: BitDelta and DeltaZip already do exactly this, and multi-LoRA serving handles adapters. Multi-tenant fine-tune hosting is a few % of inference memory, so the marginal gain is ~1x.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. If pursued, benchmark 1-bit deltas against LoRA adapters for 100 tenants of an 8B model: HBM per tenant, tokens/s and quality loss.
prior_art: BitDelta (Liu et al. 2024); DeltaZip; S-LoRA and Punica multi-adapter serving; multi-LoRA serving in vLLM.

key_insight: Binary codes in DRAM plus flash rerank cut vector-index DRAM ~25-32x at ~1-point recall loss, using popcount search on commodity CPUs.
killer_doubt: Already shipped by every major vector DB. The marginal DRAM saving over current practice is ~1x, and vector indexes are a small share of world DRAM.
decisive_experiment: None needed. At most, measure DRAM per billion vectors for binary codes plus rerank against DiskANN PQ at 95% recall@10 on a public 1B-vector benchmark.
prior_art: DiskANN (Microsoft 2019: PQ codes in DRAM, full vectors on SSD); RaBitQ (SIGMOD 2024); Elasticsearch BBQ; Qdrant and Weaviate binary quantization.

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-00308 (binary sign codes in DRAM, NVMe rerank); merge there. The 32x figure versus FP32 is right, but the practice is already deployed.
killer_doubt: In-batch duplicate of I-00308, and the market already ships it. The marginal DRAM saving over current vector-DB practice is ~1x.
prior_art: Same as I-00308: DiskANN, RaBitQ, Elasticsearch BBQ, Qdrant and Weaviate binary quantization with rescoring.

key_insight: Scoring from high planes and fetching low planes only for top-k tokens makes KV precision a fetch knob with a lossless fallback, on unchanged HBM.
killer_doubt: Gain is capped at 2x, which FP8 KV already delivers with negligible loss. NVMe low-plane fetch adds ~80-100 us per layer, ~8 ms per step over 80 layers.
decisive_experiment: On Llama-3.1-8B at 128k context, compare FP8 KV, INT4 KV and high-plane scoring with top-k low-plane fetch. Measure RULER accuracy, HBM bytes and step latency with low planes in CXL versus NVMe.
prior_art: Same mechanism as R16 I-02063 (HOLD); QuantSpec hierarchical upper/lower-nibble KV (2025); SparQ, InfiniGen and ShadowKV approximate-score fetch; vLLM FP8 KV.

key_insight: One bit-plane-major weight copy serves several precision tiers, and its MSB planes double as a free self-speculative draft model with no extra weights.
killer_doubt: Flash cannot stream low planes per step: a 70B model's 4 low planes are ~35 GB against ~14 GB/s per NVMe drive, ~2.5 s/token; the high tier is unusable.
decisive_experiment: Software only: store an 8-bit 8B model bit-plane-major, run MSB-4 as draft and all 8 planes as verifier. Measure acceptance rate, HBM bytes per token, and quality at 2-, 3- and 4-plane tiers.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (Park et al., ICML 2024) bit-plane weights; Matryoshka Quantization (Google DeepMind 2025); QuantSpec self-speculation from nested quantization.

key_insight: Per-token difficulty sets how many weight bit-planes to fetch, so easy tokens move 2-3 planes. It is worthwhile mainly for batch-1 edge decode, where weight streaming dominates.
killer_doubt: Batched serving loads each weight once per step for 32-256 tokens, so the step fetches the most planes any token needs. Untrained 2-plane truncation also degrades badly.
decisive_experiment: Train a per-token plane predictor on a nested (MatQuant-style) 8B model. Measure average planes fetched and perplexity at batch 1 and batch 64, on an edge GPU and a server GPU.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM bit-plane layout; Matryoshka Quantization nested int8/int4/int2 slices; R16 I-02063 bit-plane family.

key_insight: Session state between turns need not sit in datacenter memory. An idle session can live anywhere cheap, and a compact latent would make it portable.
killer_doubt: Exact 32k-token 70B KV is ~10 GB (MLA ~2.3 GB), so 0.5-2 MB needs ~1000x lossy gisting. Resending ~100 KB of tokens and re-prefilling already makes servers stateless.
decisive_experiment: Compress 32k-token sessions of an 8B model to 1 MB gist latents. Measure next-turn answer quality and prefill FLOPs against exact KV restore from server NVMe and against plain re-prefill.
prior_art: Stateless chat APIs that resend history; gist tokens (Mu et al. 2023); AttentionStore/CachedAttention (ATC 2024), LMCache and Mooncake KV tiers.

key_insight: Hot IDs get full learned rows while the long tail shares hashed compositional sub-tables. This matches skewed access and cuts embedding-table DRAM 10-50x.
killer_doubt: CAFE (SIGMOD 2024) already gives hot features unique rows and hashes cold ones, with migration; QR, TT-Rec and ROBE cover the tail. The marginal gain over published work is ~1x.
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. If pursued, reproduce CAFE against QR embeddings on Criteo-1TB at a fixed 0.1% AUC loss and report DRAM per model.
prior_art: QR compositional embeddings (Shi et al. 2020); CAFE (SIGMOD 2024); TT-Rec (2021); ROBE; Monolith (ByteDance) frequency-filtered hash tables.

key_insight: The GC already copies every promoted object. Packing old-gen objects into per-class columns (headers dropped, fields delta- or dictionary-coded) adds compression at near-zero extra copy cost.
killer_doubt: Old gen often holds hot caches. If the decoded working set exceeds ~30% of old gen, savings fall below 1.5x, before read-barrier costs (5-15% throughput) and write overlays.
decisive_experiment: Offline, take heap dumps and access samples from 15 Java services (Renaissance, Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Spark). Compute per-class columnar ratios and the decoded-cache size needed. ~$50k shows whether whole-heap saving clears 1.5x.
prior_art: Chen et al., heap compression during GC (OOPSLA 2003); Zippads/COCO object-based hardware compression (ASPLOS 2019); JDK compact headers (Lilliput) and string dedup.

key_insight: At 4 KB, 1% raw BER needs only ~8% parity at Shannon (~15-23% practical). Pages compressing >=1.3x carry free LDPC, giving immature cells a 1e-2 landing zone.
killer_doubt: DRAM errors cluster by row, column and chip, not iid: one dead x8 chip garbles 1/8 of a page. Each random 64 B write becomes a 4 KB read-modify-write (64x).
decisive_experiment: On an FPGA CXL board, run DDR4 rejects and DIMMs at 8-64x tREFI and 85 C, and log error maps. Replay real page traces through LZ4 plus page LDPC. Report net capacity, decode latency and uncorrectable rate.
prior_art: COP (Palframan et al., ISCA 2015); Frugal ECC (SC15) and US 8458568, compression for weak pages (via search snippet); NAND LDPC; fold into R21 I-01312.

key_insight: KV caches of different layers share aligned dominant singular vectors (xKV). One trained per-token latent with absorbed per-layer projections could cut KV capacity 10-40x, past xKV's training-free 8x.
killer_doubt: Retrofit is the doubt. Training-free xKV holds RULER only to ~8x, and beyond that single-cache designs (YOCO, LCKV) were pretrained. RoPE keys resist cross-layer sharing and weight absorption.
decisive_experiment: Distill Llama-3.1-8B into one shared 1-2k-dim latent per token with absorbed per-layer heads (~2-5B tokens, ~200 H100-hours). Measure RULER and needle accuracy at 32-128k against xKV-4 and MHA2MLA at 8x, 16x and 32x.
prior_art: xKV cross-layer SVD, 8x on Llama-3.1-8B (via search snippet); YOCO and LCKV single-cache designs; CLA; MLA (DeepSeek-V2); MHA2MLA and TransMLA retrofits.

key_insight: MXT's error was putting decompression on the cache-miss path. A CXL expander already pays ~150-250 ns, so inline LZ4 can hide there and turn a 2-3x ratio into capacity.
killer_doubt: Already being commercialized. Capacity depends on the data: incompressible or encrypted pages (~1.0x) overflow the advertised 2-3x and force OS ballooning, the integration problem that kept MXT niche.
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. A user would benchmark a shipping compressed CXL expander on fleet page traces for effective ratio, tail latency and overflow events under 10% incompressible churn.
prior_art: IBM MXT (2000-01); IBM POWER Active Memory Expansion with on-chip compression; ZeroPoint Technologies compressed-memory IP; commercial CXL compression controllers (screener note).
